questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How astronauts train for long space missions on Earth
Why workers in offices around the world go on strike
A disagreement between Skylab astronauts and mission control
How spiders manage to spin their webs inside a spacecraft
questions.why: They discuss the 1973 disagreement between the Skylab crew and mission control over their workload.

questions.q: Why does Georgina act like a bossy manager at the start?
options: Because Neil wrote a bad report
Because she is really Neil's boss
Because Neil went on strike
To show what being micromanaged is like
questions.why: Her detailed orders lead Neil to explain micromanagement, when a boss controls every small detail.

questions.q: What were the Skylab crew asked to study?
options: Many things, including spiders' webs
Only the stars and planets near Earth
How to repair the space station
The weather on Earth
questions.why: They were asked to study everything, from effects on the human body to how spiders make webs.

questions.q: According to Ed Gibson, how much instruction did they receive one morning?
options: A short radio message from mission control
About 60 feet of teleprinter message
Six pages of emails to read before lunch
A one-hour phone call with their boss
questions.why: He says one morning they had about 60 feet of teleprinter message to divide up.

questions.q: Why did Ed Gibson feel the micromanagement was a problem?
options: It made the mission too short to finish
It stopped them sleeping
They couldn't use their own judgement
It made them feel lonely
questions.why: He says they weren't getting things done as they should because they couldn't use their own judgement.

questions.q: Why did some NASA bosses think the astronauts had gone on strike?
options: All three of them missed the daily radio meeting
They refused to do any experiments
They sent an angry letter
They turned off the space station's power
questions.why: Georgina says one day all three missed the daily radio meeting and some bosses thought they'd gone on strike.

questions.q: What happened after the crisis talks?
options: The astronauts were sent back to Earth early
They agreed to work together better
The newspapers apologised
NASA gave the crew more work
questions.why: Neil says both sides agreed better ways of working and communicating, with less micromanagement.

questions.q: According to Ed Gibson, when is micromanagement actually needed?
options: During experiments
At meal times
Never
During lift-off or re-entry
questions.why: He says micromanagement doesn't work, except in situations like a lift-off or a re-entry.
